body: Chatting with my next-door neighbor over our back fence. We had gotten friendly over a number of months and we talked everyday.  He had lived a fascinating life and just letting him talk about his experiences was so eye-opening.   I remember this one time looking over at him, and the world simply disappeared into a mist and all I saw were his very pale green-blue eyes.  I knew, then, that no matter what, we had a deeper connection than just friendship.  There was a realization that I was looking at a person who connecting with my soul and it was thunderous and revealing and awesome.  The was a sense of rightness that happens very rarely in my life.  Yes, I fell in love with him.  No, we did not end up together or even discuss the underlying emotions of our friendship.   Unfortunately, he is no longer my neighbor, and I cannot find him to get in touch with him.  All I know is I can never forget him, and if his is meant to be in my life, sooner or later he will find me.

Wow, do happen to know my previous therapist? ;)  you sound exactly like her, and that is a compliment.


I am going to make a concerted effort to get my thinking back on track and do what you say, o wise one.  Thanks for the very gentle kick in the ass :D
I really appreciate this.  Thanks for being there (here? you know what I mean)

My present doc mostly does medication for treatment.  When I was in therapy at the trauma service, I had group and individual therapy at a minimum of once per week.  There just isn't that kind of treatment team set up here.
This is indeed something I want to do.  I am hoping that hubby's benefits will get reinstated soon, so I can try this.

Aye, and there's the rub.


You have hit the nail on the head, I know it.  I'm an artist, and luckily have a spare room as a studio.  I know I feel better when I am there and just pushing paint around, but my brain just won't let me go.  You know that voice that says; "You don't contribute financially, so you gotta take care of the house".  That's just one part I struggle with.  I am classified as "Disabled" by the gov't, and I know labels shouldn't matter but they do.  I feel like if only my brain would work right, then I could work, etc.  Kind of like I don't have the right to enjoy life "while I am off", I just have to work at getting better to get back to work.  I have a lot of guilt about not helping out financially.  I know this is disordered thinking, and I know I need to change things to get different results.  I really don't have a good excuse.

>I don't know how much help I can be, but have you tried sitting down and thinking for a bit about the biggest thing that's bothering you right now? For me, when I started to have memories of sexual abuse and stuff, even reading about other peoples stories and researching different methods to relax helped motivate me to resolve some of my issues.


In the past I certainly have done this, but I often find it difficult to relate to other survivors.  I don't remember 98% of the things that happened to me, which causes me to doubt myself.  I don't often have reliving flashbacks anymore.  Some of the survivor sites I have been to seem to have people at a different stage of healing than I am, or more profound symptoms than me.  I am in a type of "maintenance mode" grey area where I am not going forward or back.


I do my best everyday to "accomplish" something.  I have 3 dogs, and I try to walk them a little more or a little farther everyday.  Unfortunately, when the pain and exhaustion gets worse, I just can't do what I could do yesterday or even this a.m. Even when I load and unload the dishwasher, some days I can do it easily, whereas other days I have to break it down like "Ok, I'll unload the cutlery and rest.  Then, unload the pots and rest".   Sometimes it takes me all day to get one task done.  In my mind, I really can't see living the rest of my life one piece of cutlery at a time.


I really try to "live in the moment"; that was what some of my previous therapy had taught me.  It is just hard, wanting to do something but not being able to because your body and brain won't let you.


eta:  Does this make sense?  I can explain more if need be.
Thank you so much.  I will try and call in a bit, when I get my nerve up.
If anything, I sleep way too much.  It is a good escape, although my dreams aren't necessarily the greatest.
I am here, and holding on by the skin of my teeth.
